result: pass within the reviewed static contract; no open actionable discrepancy
scope: Independent semantic review of reference identity, rate/format ownership and grouped read/seek, plus original-image custody checks for all retained peer intervals. Not a complete independent reconstruction of every callback or sample kernel.
verification_method: Parsed the original arm64 Mach-O LC_SEGMENT_64 commands independently to translate virtual addresses into file offsets; verified the full original SHA256.

Checked every one of the 54 retained native intervals against original instruction words; separately compared all returned REA byte ranges and required each REA instruction address to lie in its original interval.
Rechecked all 521 local and 19 external manifest identities, then original dispatch/linkage spans. Author verification output was not used as the sole byte authority.

semantic_checks.result: The first collected event pointer overwrites X23 before the loop. Equality with each enumerated event supplies W3; only true reference flags store group+0x38. The final finding correctly withdraws the earlier incoming-requested-event interpretation.
The collector clears count<=1 and retains count>1. This supports at least two collected entries for this fresh group branch, while leaving collection membership and ordering unresolved.

Manager rate follows selected reference index into its stored stream. Each freshly constructed member AudioAccessor is assigned that rate through +0xf0 and reference formatID through +0x198. No project/device rate argument appears in the constructor. This is an accessor configuration/conversion boundary, not proof of all successful output samples or arbitrary callback invariance.

Curve/inversion expose Float32 with input-rate delegation. The fallback holder constructs an input AudioAccessor, configures Float32 format and seeks zero without the actual +0xf0 rate setter; its rate query delegates to that accessor. These paths do not establish project-rate conformance or prove every possible replacement stream preserves original file format.

Every member receives the supplied read count. Negative results retain the last negative result; nonnegative short reads do not reduce the returned request count. Seek adds stored member offset and retains persistent accessors; negative seek results narrow to signed32 before final sign extension. The finding correctly excludes a faithful stateless PCM/reset/EOF implementation from these facts.

Original table cells corroborate the named rate/format, group reader and actual accessor rate-setter bindings. The peer correctly keeps inner reference integer-format conversion distinct from outer Float32 wrapper exposure.

application_implication: Keep differing-rate native placed playback gated. The reviewed group conversion uses a first-collected source reference, not a demonstrated project/engine target. Existing explicit application conversion policies are not promoted to native ordinary routing by this finding.

next_discriminating_edges.question: Determine group collection ordering and eligibility before assigning semantic identity to the reference event.
Determine whether prepared/pitch replacement streams can already conform to a downstream rate before the ordinary reader; preserve cached-state conditions.
Close builder root provider and alternate channel mapping state separately; neither peer study establishes source/engine equality.

limitations: No proprietary execution, fresh Ghidra import, target audio or runtime comparison was performed for this review.
All peer intervals received custody checks; detailed independent semantic review is limited to the listed paths.
Eleven supplied-state analytical controls were read as discriminators, not relabeled as native observations.
Typed provider replacements, external registration callbacks, general warp/group PCM and historical cached states remain explicit boundaries.
Local private evidence references do not imply publishing proprietary images, raw slices or decompiler output.
